Q: How to prevent Visual Studio from automatically killing child process A:

I found the setting. It was actually a ReSharper popup, not a native Visual Studio one. Resharper has Test Runner options and this is where you can configure to leave the spawned processes running.

Q: How to confirm web app is running in .NET 10 A:

One way to find out for sure is to use Azure App Services' "Kudu" SCM webpage, which will show you exactly what DLLs are loaded into your w3wp.exe worker-process instances, and from there, you can see which version of .NET you're using:

  1. Go to https://your-site-name.scm.azurewebsites.net (note the .scm. DNS label).
  2. Go to Process Explorer ( https://your-site-name.scm.azurewebsites.net/ProcessExplorer/ )
  3. Look for the w3wp.exe instance without the blue "SCM" label, click "Properties".
  4. Click the "Modules" tab.
  5. Scroll down to look for names like "System.Private.CoreLib.dll" or "System.Core.dll".
  6. Note the version-number displayed.

Q: AEC Data Model - Phase Information for Elements A:

Morning gents,

I have an issue with room phases too but my issue is that one of my models is missing the Phase reference property for 6x rooms out of 126x. I've already compared all the properties from the 6x rooms against properties of some of the "good" rooms and nothing stood out. The 6x rooms:

  • Are placed and have a valid area

  • Have no warnings, overlapping rooms or are redundant

  • Are not part of a design option or groups

  • Show the phase in Revit Lookup within Revit just like a "good" room

  • Have no other properties (or reference properties) that resemble a Phase property

  • Don't seem to have an autodesk.revit.parameter:roomPhase-4.0.0 property id (or a 1.0.0) like the "good" rooms do, also not sure why the Revit API shows 1.0.0 but the Data Model shows 4.0.0

  • Are not on a level or phase that hasn't been extracted for other similar rooms

Any ideas?

At the moment I'm doing other tests like deleting and replacing the room, auditing the model, etc, etc, to see if any of that will affect the outcome.
